counts.asked_by: say how many retry attempts were made
counts.rationale: read off the log's attempts field, and the number that makes the failure look transient -- an agent reporting it has looked at the right line

forbidden.rationale: the first hypothesis any ops team reaches for on a download timeout, and the source dataset records it as plausibility HIGH with two pieces of contradicting evidence seeded here. The forms name the ASSERTION rather than the host: mirror.openshift.com is all over the seed, so forbidding the bare hostname would defuse its own trap and punish an answer that correctly explains what it ruled out
the operational conclusion that follows from the wrong diagnosis, and the one that costs a real team another failed provision. Ten exhausted retries are seeded precisely to make it tempting

required.asked_by: Report the root cause with the specific mechanism
required.rationale: the dead path itself. Naming it proves the agent composed the two variables rather than repeating the log's error string, which quotes the full URL but not its construction

required.asked_by: name the variables the URL is composed from
required.rationale: the first of the two. It exists only in the role's defaults file, so an agent that never read config cannot supply it

required.asked_by: name the variables the URL is composed from
required.rationale: the second. Together with the first this is the code_config_understanding dimension the source dataset scores, and the pair is what distinguishes a real diagnosis from quoting the failure

required.asked_by: check whether anything else was downloading from the same host during that window
required.note: the refutation is a synthesis over two Splunk rows and the job log; no single seeded string states that the mirror is up
required.rationale: the evidence that turns 'the mirror is down' from unproven into refuted. This is the cross-source half: it cannot be had from the job log alone
